source.title: Effect of atmospheric pressure plasma treatments for enhanced adhesion of arc-sprayed zinc coatings on CFRP substrates
source.publisher: Composites Part A: Applied Science and Manufacturing

process_summary.plasma_regime: atmospheric-pressure air and argon plasma pretreatment
process_summary.failure_analysis: ImageJ analysis of zinc-peeled/fractured CFRP surfaces

substrate_profile.matrix_resin_system: SIGRAPREG epoxy resin system developed by SGL Carbon

reported_morphology_condition_example.qualifier: Explicitly described morphology condition; not claimed as the best-performing condition or a recommended recipe.

mechanisms_reported: Argon plasma ablated some surface epoxy and exposed carbon fibres, supporting mechanical interlocking.
Air plasma generated oxygen-rich –OH / –COOH groups and increased polar surface energy; authors discuss interaction with ZnO species.

reported_observations.qualifier: most intense air-plasma condition reported by the study

unknowns_and_blockers: Exact commercial CFRP laminate grade, fibre grade, prepreg batch/lot, fibre volume fraction, cure history and coupon-to-panel variability remain to be extracted.

The full air/argon process matrix, exact winning condition and treatment repeatability must be reconstructed from complete methods/results tables; Air_30_10 is one described morphology condition only.

The paper discusses grit blasting as a topography-changing process, but whether grit blasting was applied to every comparison arm and the exact treatment sequence must be verified from the full methods.
Exact plasma article, process gas purity/flow, nozzle, traverse/speed, power measurement boundary, waveform and treatment-to-spray delay are not fully established by indexed methods excerpts.
Exact zinc wire/feedstock grade/lot, arc-spray equipment identity, spray distance, electrical parameters, deposition rate, coating thickness and post-treatment require full methods extraction.

Exact pull-off standard, fixture/dolly geometry, adhesive, cure, loading rate, specimen dimensions, replicate count, censoring/invalid specimens and failure-area classification are not established by the accessible abstract/indexed record.
Raw replicate-level adhesion values and the construction of ±0.12 MPa uncertainty are not yet reconstructed.
Grid-to-coating energy, gas/extraction loads and lifecycle costs are not established.
No LSP, aircraft qualification, certification, lightning-current performance or post-strike structural claim is established.

source.title: Characterization and evaluation of plasma-sprayed coatings on polymeric substrates

cases.source_limitation: Abstract identifies further process optimization and long-term durability as necessary; no universal coating performance is inferred.

negative_controls.claim: 4.21 MPa pull-off adhesion establishes LSP compliance
assume the source pull-off test was ASTM C633 or ASTM D4541 without checking its methods
higher coating adhesion is beneficial even if resin recession/fibre damage violates laminate requirements
different CFRP resin systems/layups/lots can be pooled without stratification
contact angle or surface energy alone proves conductive coating adhesion
adhesion results establish electrical continuity or current-carrying capability
discharge power is the complete grid-to-service energy boundary
a CZM simulation output is a measured interface strength

standards_crosswalk.role: aircraft lightning environment and related test waveforms
aircraft lightning direct-effects and indirect-effects test methods; authority approves damage/pass criteria
composite aircraft structure guidance; lightning effectiveness demonstrated by tests or analysis supported by tests
thermal-spray coating adhesion/cohesion test; coupon-level comparison only
portable pull-off test whose scope is coatings on metal substrates; do not assume suitability for CFRP or source-paper method

interface_design_hypotheses.description: Test whether a separately identified sequence/spatially selective treatment can combine mechanical interlocking associated with epoxy recession/fibre exposure and chemical functionalization associated with polar surface groups while preserving laminate properties.

spatial_interface_metrology_hypothesis.description: Co-register local surface chemistry, resin/fibre exposure, topography, coating thickness/defects, sheet resistance and destructive adhesion/failure sites to predict local conductive-coating failure and substrate damage on held-out panels/lots.
